_comment: How a ship's dimensions and armour scheme are turned into internal geometry. The same generator runs for a historical preset and for a player design, which is what stops the combat engine from ever needing to know the difference.

hull._depthToDraftComment: Keel-to-main-deck depth as a multiple of draft. Sets freeboard, and with it how much of the belt is above water and how much side a shell can strike.
hull._beltTopComment: The main belt's top edge meets the armoured deck: together they are the citadel, a box of vertical plate closed by a horizontal one. The side above the armoured deck is covered by the upper belt where a design has one.
hull._superstructureComment: Height of the superstructure above the main deck, as a fraction of length.
hull._beltBottomComment: How far below the waterline the main belt reaches, as a fraction of draft. Belts extended well under water precisely because shells fall short and travel on.
hull._beltTaperComment: Fraction of the belt's height, measured down from its top, that carries the full stated thickness. Below it the plate tapers to the scheme's lowerEdgeThicknessMm. Belts were thick around the waterline and thin at the bottom, where the strake catches shells that fell short and travelled on underwater rather than resisting a direct hit.
hull._armourDeckComment: Depth of the main armoured deck below the main deck, as a fraction of draft.

citadel._comment: The armoured box. Derived from where the main battery sits, because the citadel exists to cover the magazines and the machinery between them.

compartments._comment: Resolution of the internal subdivision. Higher numbers give finer damage localisation at proportionally more tracing cost. Fourteen stations puts a compartment boundary roughly every 19 m on a battleship and every 8 m on a destroyer, which is about right for both.

permeability._comment: Fraction of a compartment's volume that floods when it is opened to the sea. Machinery spaces are full of machinery; voids are empty by design.

structuralContribution._comment: How much each compartment's destruction costs the hull girder, relative to its volume. Machinery and magazine spaces sit inside the citadel and carry the ship's strength; end compartments carry much less. This is what makes structural integrity a DERIVED figure rather than a counter.
structuralContribution._aboveMainDeckComment: Multiplier applied to anything standing above the main deck. The hull girder is the hull; the superstructure rides on it, and deckhouses were often given expansion joints so the hull could bend without tearing them. Wrecking a bridge costs a ship her fire control, and a funnel shot through costs her draught — neither costs her structure.

crew._comment: How the ship's company is distributed, as a share of total crew. Drives casualties: a shell into a manned machinery space kills more people than one into a void.
